paper.title: RoboReward: General-Purpose Vision-Language Reward Models for Robotics
paper.source_version: arXiv v2, revised 2026-01-08; latest public arXiv version verified 2026-08-31; PDF SHA-256 601200a96f8e30137cd3166d6d330ff9ff2ceb0de6a4c43949d808e6e9c0d29a. Official artifacts are pinned to HELM suite v0.0.1, dataset commit 469b9af76e8539e8d2ac553b081307738fd92ca5, 4B checkpoint commit 4dec8af8d89d214de7028d70f9f9aee3b3a44c3d, and 8B checkpoint commit 3a185b4fce2b1253643105be1f234ae618b9732f.

decision_relevance.why_admitted: RoboReward supplies a transferable episodic vision-language scoring interface, a human-verified robot reward benchmark, controlled negative and near-miss construction, and fixed-DSRL comparisons that separate the learned training reward from final binary task success.
not_evidence_for: executable task-reward code over simulator state or action fields
reference composition, mode discovery, phase-window dispatch, or closed-loop oracle logic
a dense per-step reward, long-horizon credit assignment, or multi-stage progress estimation
an objective evaluator when the same model output is optimized as training reward or candidate-selection feedback
human-calibrated ground truth beyond one-reviewer accept/reject verification of the benchmark test split
a reward-form- and scale-matched comparison between binary human labels and five-level VLM scores
statistically replicated real-robot RL results across training seeds
portability across parameterized MDPs, trainers, policy architectures, robots, or observation/action contracts

mechanisms.name: Instruction-conditioned episodic progress model
mechanisms.description: A vision-language model consumes a natural-language task and full robot rollout video and emits one discrete end-of-episode progress score in {1,2,3,4,5}; it does not consume simulator state/action fields or emit executable reward code.

mechanisms.name: Counterfactual instruction relabeling
mechanisms.description: For a successful score-5 video, the pipeline holds the video fixed and generates alternative imperative commands whose final-state satisfaction forms calibrated score levels 1 through 4, testing instruction-sensitive failure and near-miss discrimination.

mechanisms.name: Temporal clipping for grounded partial progress
mechanisms.description: The pipeline holds the original successful command fixed and clips the same rollout to earlier endpoints, assigning score levels 1 through 4 to create visually grounded partial-progress outcomes.

mechanisms.name: Rubric-constrained generation and rejection teacher
mechanisms.description: GPT-5 mini analyzes sampled video frames, plans strictly ordered failures, and validates generated triples; Qwen3-4B emits one constrained command per score. Inconsistent or ungrounded triples are rejected before model training.

mechanisms.name: Human-verified held-out reward benchmark
mechanisms.description: RoboRewardBench contains 2,831 task-video-label triples whose generated or organic scores were accepted by one human reviewer; 22 VLMs are compared by group-wise mean absolute error across source subsets.

mechanisms.name: Fixed-DSRL external reward comparison
mechanisms.description: On two WidowX tasks, the same DSRL policy-improvement setup and 6,000-step budget receive either binary human success, RoboReward 8B progress, or Gemini Robotics-ER progress; final policy performance is reported separately as binary success over 20 trials.

mechanisms.name: Versioned benchmark, dataset, and model releases
mechanisms.description: The official project links a HELM leaderboard, a 54,135-row task-video-score dataset, and Qwen3-VL 4B/8B checkpoints; the 8B model card documents the five-level inference prompt.

failure_modes.name: High-impact visual false positives and negatives
failure_modes.description: The paper shows Gemini Robotics-ER assigning 5/5 to a closed-drawer failure, 2/5 to a successful opening, and 5/5 to a monkey apparently hovering rather than resting on a towel; the associated descriptions hallucinate or miss decisive temporal and spatial events.

failure_modes.name: Non-uniform embodiment and source generalization
failure_modes.description: RoboReward 8B is best overall but reports MAE 1.394 on UTokyo xArm Bimanual and 0.890 on Stanford HYDRA; the best HYDRA model reports 0.495, so aggregate rank does not guarantee reliable per-domain scoring.

failure_modes.name: Single-reviewer benchmark verification
failure_modes.description: Each test example is accepted or rejected by one reviewer; no inter-rater agreement, reviewer calibration, or adjudication procedure is reported, limiting the strength of the human-verified label claim.

failure_modes.name: Synthetic label and validator dependence
failure_modes.description: GPT-5 mini both helps construct and validates augmented labels; the authors state generated labels are not guaranteed correct, and human verification is applied only to the test split rather than all training supervision.

failure_modes.name: MAE hides reward-hacking risk asymmetry
failure_modes.description: Group-wise MAE averages absolute score distance and does not separately report catastrophic false-positive and false-negative rates; over-rewarding a failure can be more damaging under policy optimization than an equally sized benign error.

failure_modes.name: Human-versus-VLM reward form confound
failure_modes.description: The real-robot human condition supplies binary {0,1} success while VLM conditions supply progress {1,...,5}; matched DSRL hyperparameters therefore do not isolate label-source quality from reward shaping and numerical scale.

failure_modes.name: Unreported RL-training replication uncertainty
failure_modes.description: Real-robot success is reported over 20 final trials per condition, but the paper does not report repeated RL-training seeds or confidence intervals, so training variance is not quantified.

failure_modes.name: Offline-MAE correlation is not a universal guarantee
failure_modes.description: The reported r=0.83 association pools checkpoints across three simulation tasks without a confidence interval; it does not establish that reducing held-out MAE will causally improve every downstream RL setting.

failure_modes.name: Task-string split does not prove scene or embodiment transfer
failure_modes.description: Train, validation, and test are disjoint by original task description, but the paper does not report grouping by scene, source dataset, or embodiment, leaving stricter transfer questions unresolved.

failure_modes.name: Short-horizon episodic scope
failure_modes.description: The method scores complete short-horizon episodes and explicitly leaves longer-horizon, multi-stage progress estimation and credit assignment to future work.

failure_modes.name: Total-versus-generated example wording inconsistency
failure_modes.description: The introduction says the augmentation pipeline yields all 54,135 examples, while the dataset method and source table use 54,135 for the complete mixture, which includes original OXE demonstrations and organic RoboArena episodes.

evaluation.name: Binary versus continuous and discrete progress reward study
evaluation.description: Across Lift, Can, and Square Robomimic tasks with three seeds, learned continuous and five-bin progress rewards converge faster and nearly match simulator-ground-truth binary reward, while the learned binary reward performs worse; curves rather than exact terminal values are reported.

evaluation.name: Held-out reward MAE versus downstream success
evaluation.description: Across checkpoints and three Robomimic tasks, reward accuracy measured offline is associated with converged true task success at r=0.83.

evaluation.name: RoboRewardBench group-wise MAE evaluation
evaluation.description: Twenty-two VLMs predict five-level final-state progress on 2,831 human-verified task-video examples; RoboReward 8B ranks first at 0.665 group-wise MAE and RoboReward 4B ranks fourth at 0.845.

evaluation.name: Organic and synthetic negative-data ablation
evaluation.description: For RoboReward 4B, removing all negative augmentation changes overall/RoboArena MAE from 0.845/0.806 to 1.450/0.797, and removing clipping changes it to 1.075/0.813, isolating broad-coverage benefits outside the organic RoboArena subset.

evaluation.name: Separate binary success after reward-driven real-robot RL
evaluation.description: With matched DSRL settings and 6,000 steps, RoboReward 8B yields 50% and 80% success on pick-and-place monkey and open drawer, versus 10% and 45% for Gemini Robotics-ER and 75% and 90% for binary human reward, each measured over 20 final trials.

evaluation.name: Fine-state false-reward audit
evaluation.description: Three Gemini Robotics-ER rollouts expose false success, false failure, and hover-versus-place errors, linking score failures to hallucinated grasps, missed drawer motion, and hallucinated release.

evidence.locator: arXiv v2 metadata/header and Introduction contribution list; revised 2026-01-08
evidence.claim: The active v2 record identifies the title, six authors, revision date, project URL, 54,135-example statement, 2,831-episode benchmark, 14 embodiment types, and 22 evaluated VLMs.

evidence.locator: Section 3 and Figure 2, The Role of Reward in Reinforcement Learning
evidence.claim: The study restricts RoboReward to full-episode rewards, defines binary, continuous-progress, and five-bin discrete-progress signals, and compares learned variants using DSRL-NA on three Robomimic tasks over three seeds with true simulator success as policy performance.

evidence.locator: Section 3, Figure 3 and adjacent paragraph
evidence.claim: Across reward-model checkpoints and all three Robomimic tasks, held-out reward accuracy and converged downstream RL success have reported correlation r=0.83.

evidence.locator: Section 4.1, Data Sources
evidence.claim: OXE supplies successful demonstrations subsampled to at most 1,200 episodes per source and assigned score 5, while RoboArena supplies organic successes and failures whose human progress in [0,100] is mapped to scores 1-5.

evidence.locator: Section 4.2, Negative Example Generation
evidence.claim: Counterfactual relabeling keeps video fixed while changing the task, and negative clipping keeps task fixed while ending a successful trajectory earlier, producing failure and partial-progress examples without fabricated video.

evidence.locator: Section 4.2, Rubric and Validation
evidence.claim: A fixed five-level final-state rubric and VLM-based coherence/score check filter examples; the authors call the teacher pipeline too costly for an RL loop and state its labels are not guaranteed perfect.

evidence.locator: Section 4.3, Training and Evaluation of General-Purpose Robot Reward Models
evidence.claim: The corpus contains 45,072 train, 6,232 validation, and 2,831 test examples split by original task description; Qwen3-VL 4B/8B freeze vision and train fusion/LLM layers for three epochs with the stated optimizer hyperparameters and select by validation MAE.

evidence.locator: Section 5.1 and Table 1, Benchmarking frontier VLMs with RoboRewardBench
evidence.claim: Twenty-two VLMs receive task descriptions and rollout videos, emit labels 1-5, and are ranked by group-wise MAE on the human-verified benchmark.

evidence.locator: Section 5.1 and Appendix B.2, Tables 7 and 10
evidence.claim: RoboReward 8B ranks first at 0.665 overall MAE and RoboReward 4B fourth at 0.845; tables report base-model, frontier-model, RoboArena, and per-source results, including non-uniform RoboReward 8B subset errors.

evidence.locator: Section 5.2, Setting
evidence.claim: The real-robot test uses a WidowX 250 6-DoF arm, BridgeData V2-pretrained multi-task diffusion policy, DSRL, two unseen tasks, 6,000 steps, 70-step episode cap, and human-binary versus RoboReward/Gemini five-level end-of-episode reward conditions; both VLMs are zero-shot.

evidence.locator: Section 5.2, Table 2 and Results
evidence.claim: Over 20 final trials per task and condition, pick-and-place success is base 5%, human 75%, RoboReward 50%, Gemini Robotics-ER 10%; drawer success is 10%, 90%, 80%, and 45%, respectively.

evidence.locator: Section 5.3, Table 3, Data Mixture Ablations
evidence.claim: For the 4B model, full data scores 0.845 overall/0.806 RoboArena MAE; removing all negative augmentation scores 1.450/0.797; removing clipping scores 1.075/0.813.

evidence.locator: Section 6, Discussion
evidence.claim: The authors report large non-uniform generalization gaps and identify longer-horizon, multi-stage reward modeling with harder credit assignment and progress estimation as future work.

evidence.locator: Appendix A.1, Table 4, Dataset Sources
evidence.claim: The source table totals 54,135 examples and gives per-source train, validation, and test counts, including RoboArena at 7,337/1,000/1,000.

evidence.locator: Appendix A.2.2-A.2.3, Negative Example Generation and Verification prompts
evidence.claim: The teacher uses GPT-5 mini for 1-FPS video analysis, failure planning, and validation; Qwen3-4B generates under-25-word imperative commands; generated and clipped examples target labels 1-4 with strict ordering and are rejected when inconsistent.

evidence.locator: Appendix A.3, Human Verification for RoboRewardBench
evidence.claim: One human annotator reviews each test video, task, label, rubric, and automated rationale; mismatches are discarded before subsampling the 2,831-example benchmark.

evidence.locator: Appendix B.3 and Figure 6, Pitfalls of State-of-the-Art VLMs
evidence.claim: Three Gemini Robotics-ER failures include a 5/5 closed drawer, 2/5 successful opening, and 5/5 hovering monkey; detailed descriptions reveal hallucinated or missed task-defining temporal and spatial events.

evidence.locator: Appendix B.4 and Tables 8-9, Real-World RL Experiment
evidence.claim: All reward conditions use the same DSRL-SAC hyperparameters, the replay buffer starts with 20 base-policy rollouts, and the appendix specifies base diffusion-policy and WidowX DSRL settings.

evidence.locator: Official HELM RoboReward project landing page, suite v0.0.1
evidence.claim: The official project links the paper, full leaderboard, dataset, and 4B/8B checkpoint repositories.

evidence.locator: Pinned official 8B model card; cross-checked against official dataset card at commit 469b9af76e8539e8d2ac553b081307738fd92ca5
evidence.claim: The released 8B checkpoint is based on Qwen3-VL-8B and its model card specifies the task-video prompt and five-level end-of-episode score; the pinned dataset card documents 54,135 rows, split sizes, fields, and human-verified test status.
